disease_label_per_paper: ESBL-producing bacterial orbital cellulitis with facial cellulitis in pulmonary tuberculosis
presentation_summary: A 47-year-old man was referred with swollen and painful right eye and face for 8 days; the swelling worsened and pus appeared 3 days before admission.
He had toothache for 2 years and bloody cough for 5 months; no trauma history was found.
On admission he was drowsy, pale, and febrile.
Right eye visual acuity was light perception only and eye movement was limited in all directions.

Exam showed non-axial proptosis, upper and lower eyelid swelling with purulent discharge, chemosis, purulent conjunctival discharge, hazy cornea, and a right mandibular-to-inner-buccal fistula releasing pus.
CT showed orbital sub-tissue swelling and subperiosteal abscess on the upper lateral orbital wall.
Laboratory testing was described as leukocytosis with elevated ESR.

procedures.source_text_value: managed with irrigation and drainage of the abscess once a day

actual_treatment.name: after culture, intravenous ampicillin-sulbactam plus intravenous metronidazole
planned fixed-dose combination therapy for pulmonary tuberculosis

clinical_course.description: Despite initial therapy the patient still had fever, cough, right eye and facial swelling, and active pus production.
Culture and tuberculosis testing changed the antibiotic and pulmonary treatment plan.
Swelling and abscess resolved with systemic condition improvement.

outcome_follow_up.description: Discharged in stable systemic condition with eyelid swelling and abscess resolved.

quality_warnings: Culture organisms, ESBL status, susceptibility, AFB result, antibiotic switch, tuberculosis treatment plan, and response are post-presentation evidence and are use_in_ranking:false.
Numeric WBC and ESR values were not reported, so qualitative leukocytosis and elevated ESR are preserved without inventing exact values.
